intentionalDifferences: Phase 3 lands connection-scoped leases, opaque one-shot approvals, and AiSandbox partition selection in Electron main.
Phase 4 completes standing grants, attachment/mode authority, human reclaim, operation guard, and user-gated production enablement without an env bypass.
Phase 2 rebuilds browser chrome in Auris's React conventions and warm mint visual system while retaining VMark-equivalent tab, omnibox, history, bookmark, approval, and crash behavior.

Canonical strict parser/schema/compiler/step vocabulary lives in packaged electron/shared/browser-workflow-contract.cjs; TypeScript modules are thin adapters. Compilation emits typed intents and approval points but grants no authority.

Phase 5 intentionally wires VMark's separately defined browser Markdown parser, runner, recorder, and self-heal cores into a runtime, with per-attempt reauthorization and review instead of treating the upstream experimental core as complete.

Task 8 runs only main-reparsed Markdown against an explicit window/tab, reacquires and releases dispatcher control for every step/approval retry, binds imported-source review separately from execution authority, and confines API steps to freshly authorized bounded HTTPS requests without ambient cookies.

Task 9 records only trusted main/browser outcomes, converts every typed value to an opaque declared input before capture, and makes target repair a bounded propose/review/recompile/fresh-authorize flow with no silent rewrite.
Phase 1 freezes shared command/error fixtures and a Node integration harness for later MCP/main-process tests.
Phase 3 exposes the closed VMark-equivalent browser action union through Auris's authenticated stdio sidecar, with authority terminating in Electron main rather than a renderer bridge.
Phase 3 proves the research loop with an explicit Electron test-app composition and real stdio MCP client.
Phase 4 composes production browserMcpDispatcher only after compiled security gates verify and the user enables MCP browser automation; named profiles/cookie replay stay independently gated.
ARIA projection, stable refs, and clean-reader live in page-observation.ts / stable-refs.ts / clean-reader.ts with explicit budgets, generation-stamped refs, and no iframe/shadow piercing.
Phase 1 ports architecture-independent TypeScript algorithms into Auris feature namespaces and keeps page observations explicitly untrusted.
URL/origin/AI-navigation policy lives in url-policy.ts; structured target canonicalization and SHA-256 payload binding live in target-descriptor.ts; Electron main still performs final authorization.
Phase 2 replaces VMark's Rust/Tauri/WKWebView surface with Electron BrowserWindow and WebContentsView while preserving stable window/tab identities and lifecycle semantics.
Named profiles and cookie/localStorage replay remain independently false in production capability defaults even after Phase 4 security gates verify.

Phase 4 maps sessions to Electron partitions and macOS Keychain-backed ciphertext refs, adds crash budgets/hibernation without authority restore, redacted diagnostics audit, and fail-closed UX policy.

Electron BrowserWindow/WebContentsView ownership replaces Tauri window routing, overlay, occlusion, and persistence shells; Auris projects a redacted main-owned status DTO and never derives authority from renderer focus or stored status.
Phase 6 adapts VMark's window status concepts to multiple independently targetable Electron browser windows plus the existing Auris main window, with explicit identity for ambiguous targets.
Phase 5 renames VMark Genie to Auris Nia, exports only canonical nia: v1 data, and retains explicit legacy v0, genie: v1, and uses: genie/* import migration.
Phase 5 replaces Rust provider execution with bounded Electron main-process CLI and REST adapters; keys remain memory-only unless the user explicitly chooses Keychain storage.

Task 1 defines the canonical/legacy Markdown+frontmatter contract in a packaged CJS module with strict YAML (core schema, zero aliases, depth/size bounds) so main always reparses raw source instead of trusting a renderer-supplied AST.

Task 2 adds a canonical/legacy-aware definition repository: immutable built-ins plus an injected-baseDir filesystem store that reparses raw source through the packaged contract, writes via temp-file-plus-rename, and always displays provenance/labels as Nia while resolving both nia/<name> and legacy genie/<name> references to the same canonical identity.

Task 3 adds secure provider configuration: REST/CLI metadata persisted separately from secrets, process-memory REST keys by default, explicit rememberOnThisMac writing opaque nia-provider Keychain references, exactly one active default, and rejection of user executable/flags/shell/env/cwd plus non-HTTPS remote endpoints.

Task 4 executes providers only through fixed, bounded main-process adapters: HTTPS/loopback-only REST transports and shell:false audited Claude, Codex, and Gemini CLI registrations with prompt-on-stdin, isolated temporary cwd, minimal environment, cancellation, output caps, and sender-bound narrow IPC.

Task 5 mounts one sanitized warm-mint Nia surface in browser chrome and Notes, attaches browser/note/workflow context only after explicit user action, and applies Notes proposals only after revision and selection review; local conversation history remains opt-in.
Phase 5 ports the wired VMark YAML pipeline engine as the distinct Nia workflow family, canonicalizing uses: nia/* while accepting the legacy Genie alias.

Task 10 exposes both workflow families through one owner-bound main facade and additive auris_workflow MCP/UI surfaces; list/inspect/validate remain pure while each family's start capability stays independently smoke-gated.

The packaged CJS contract is the only parser, schema, registry, dependency scheduler, and runner; TypeScript files are thin adapters. Main reparses raw YAML, owns run identity/cancellation, rejects renderer AST/action/token claims, and routes allowlisted action/* effects through an injected approval/review service.
Phase 1 stores the upstream ISC notice verbatim in UPSTREAM-LICENSE.txt; README.md adds Auris provenance context and a non-endorsement disclaimer.
Phase 6 retains manual upstream review: the report never rewrites Auris source or silently changes the pinned provenance baseline.
The deterministic read-only comparison report is generated from the pinned baseline and records the separately reviewed current comparison commit.

Preserve Auris browser and Nia workflow semantics while separating tools by risk, attaching annotations and structured errors, and binding mutating authority to verified installed-client principals.
The five-session xterm core is aligned; file-path navigation, suspend/resume, and full session restoration follow after durable recovery.
